scenario.name: Microsoft SQL Server Security, Mandiant & MITRE T1505.001 — MSSQL Linked Server RPC, xp_cmdshell & Unsafe CLR Assembly Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a chain of corporate record rooms connected by internal brass pneumatic tubes that automatically stamp every parcel with chief-archivist clearance at the far end. An intruder inspects the directory to spot which pneumatic tubes carry top clearance, flips two restricted control switches on the remote room’s wall to unlock its maintenance hatch, and loads a custom mechanical helper directly into the record ledger without ever leaving a physical tool box on the floor. In this scenario (T1021, Microsoft SQL Server Security, Mandiant & MITRE T1505.001, MSSQL Linked Server RPC, xp_cmdshell & Unsafe CLR Assembly Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mSSQL Linked Server Enumeration, then configuration Change Enabling xp_cmdshell, then in-Memory Hexadecimal CLR Assembly. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MSSQL Linked Server Enumeration, then Configuration Change Enabling xp_cmdshell, then In-Memory Hexadecimal CLR Assembly, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 33205 correlated across the documented kill chain.
